newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RTRS-Rugby union-Campese saves Australian blushes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rugby union-Campese saves Australian blushes.

text.p: Winger David Campese, playing his last tournament in an Australian shirt, saved the Wallabies from defeat in their opening game against Scotland in the World Cup Sevens on Friday.

Campese, the leading try scorer in international rugby with 64, came on as substitute with Australia trailing 19-5 in the second half but his influence, including the final try which he converted himself, helped salvage a 19-19 draw in the pool B encounter.

"This is definitely the last time I play for Australia," said Campese, who has been capped 101 times for his country at 15-a-side. "I love playing in Hong Kong and I wanted to come as this is the World Cup and people are watching to see how Australia perform.
"We have a very young side and we were a bit nervous to start. We put ourselves in a difficult position by letting them get ahead of us. We cannot afford to do that but at least we did not lose."
Scotland had gone ahead thanks to two tries from 20-year-old winger James Craig, whose father Jim was in the Celtic soccer side which won the European Cup in 1967.

"It was great to get a couple of scores," said the fleet-footed Craig, who has a best 100 metres time of 10.8 seconds. "My dad encouraged me to play another sport as he thought he would be too pushy if I played soccer."

Australia, runners-up to England in the first World Cup Sevens in 1993, were playing Romania later in the day. The pool play on the first day is essentially shadow boxing as the teams will be ranked 1-24, based on results and tries scored, and redrawn into pools for Saturday's session.

England made a competent start to the defence of their trophy with a 33-12 win over Canada. Mike Catt had the distinction of scoring the first try in the tournament and further tries from Tim Rodber, Neil Back, David Scully and Richard Hill gave England a comfortable win.
Favourites New Zealand, winners of the Hong Kong Sevens for the past three years, opened with a straightforward 47-14 victory over 1993 World Cup Sevens Bowl winners, Japan.

New Zealand, who are missing Jonah Lomu because of a kidney ailment and the influential Christian Cullen due to injury, had to make another change to their line-up when Dallas Seymour failed a finness test on a sprained ankle before the start of play. He was replaced by Alama Ieremia, who was on standby.
